title: Smile and Hymn
premise: Ada Montrose arrives at Hollowmere Primary to replace a teacher who vanished mid-term, joining a staff that treats the school's missing-class problem as weather—unfortunate, seasonal, not to be discussed. When an excavation crew unearths a door sealed from the inside beneath the old chapel wing, Ada discovers the school was built over something that trades: every generation, it takes children, and in exchange the town prospers. The 1974 class of Hollowmere made a bargain that was never completed—one child, Miriam Voss, was meant to be returned but wasn't, and her absence has been accruing interest for fifty years. Ada, whose own grandmother was in that class, must choose between the duty she inherited and the love she's just found with the excavation foreman, ending with Ada returning not Miriam but herself, sealing the door from the inside—and discovering, in the final pages, that what waits below has been keeping all the taken children alive, waiting for someone willing to stay.
about_author: Ulyana Almeida is a former rural schoolteacher who spent six years in a village where the church records ended abruptly in 1974. She writes horror about institutions, inheritance, and the things communities agree not to see.

chapters.title: The Substitute
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She arrives at Hollowmere Primary to find her predecessor's classroom untouched—chalk mid-word, a half-graded stack of papers—and a headmaster who explains the absence with practiced smoothness. The children are polite, watchful, wrong in small ways: they flinch at the chapel bell. Emotional beat: unease disguised as professional newness; Ada notices everything and believes none of it.

chapters.title: Attendance
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The register lists eleven students; nine arrive. When she asks about the missing two, the other teachers change the subject in unison, like a chorus. She finds her predecessor's hidden notes: dates, names, tally marks counting down. Emotional beat: isolation deepens—the first crack in her rationalism, papered over with pedagogy.

chapters.title: Ground Penetrating
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with Callum Reyes, the excavation foreman restoring the chapel wing. His crew's ground radar shows a void no blueprint accounts for. Ada and Callum meet over shared skepticism of the town's silence; flirtation sparks through mutual stubbornness. Emotional beat: connection against a backdrop of institutional denial—love beginning exactly where duty gets complicated.

chapters.title: Sealed From the Inside
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. The crew breaks through to a door whose hinges are on their side—someone shut themselves in. Scratched into the iron: M. VOSS, 1974, and beneath it, dozens of smaller names. That night, the school's absent two students appear in Ada's register again, in fresh ink. Emotional beat: dread turning concrete; the past stops being metaphor.

chapters.title: What the Town Was Bought With
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. In the county archive she finds 1974's ledger: after Miriam Voss disappeared, Hollowmere received funding, jobs, a new wing—prosperity with a timestamp. Her grandmother's name is in the class photo, standing beside empty air where Miriam should be. Emotional beat: inheritance revealed as complicity; Ada realizes her family helped build this.

chapters.title: The Bell Rings Anyway
chapters.summary: Multiple POV. The chapel bell tolls though it has no rope. Children begin sleepwalking toward the excavation site; teachers stand in doorways watching, some weeping, some smiling. The headmaster finally confesses: the town renews the bargain each generation, and this year's payment is due. Emotional beat: collective guilt surfaces; the horror becomes civic, not supernatural alone.

chapters.title: Miriam
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, dream-vision. Below the door she meets Miriam Voss—not dead, preserved, ageless, keeper of the thing that waits. It doesn't want children, Miriam explains; it wants a willing heir, someone who chooses to stay. Every vanished teacher was offered the choice and refused, and refusals are paid for in students. Emotional beat: pity and terror braided together; the monster reframed as a landlord.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. He finds Ada packing to leave—her one honest escape route—and begs her to take it. She tells him about the choice, and about her grandmother's debt. They spend one real night together while the town below counts down. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh; she chooses him by choosing to leave, which makes the final reversal land harder.

chapters.title: Return What Was Taken
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. At dawn she walks the children back to their classrooms, then descends alone through the excavation. She offers herself in Miriam's place—not as sacrifice but as successor, taking the ledger, the keys, the long watch. The door closes behind her, sealed from the inside, her handprint replacing Miriam's scratched name. Emotional beat: climax as quiet volition; duty fulfilled by love, not despite it.

chapters.title: Smile and Hymn
chapters.summary: Callum's POV, epilogue. A year later: Hollowmere thrives, attendance perfect, the chapel bell silent. He teaches Sunday hymns to children who sometimes pause mid-song, listening to something under the floor. On his desk, a chalk-written note in Ada's hand: 'They were never taken. They were kept.' He smiles, and keeps teaching. Emotional beat: bittersweet resolution—corruption inherited willingly, power accepted, love enduring underground.
